newsitem.title: USA: Warm, dry weather to aid weekend US corn combining.
newsitem.headline: Warm, dry weather to aid weekend US corn combining.

text.p: Warm, dry weather over the weekend should ensure active harvesting of corn and soybeans in the U.S. Midwest, meteorologists said.

"It looks pretty good for harvesting activity in the corn belt," Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc said, noting temperatures would be in the 70s F in the western Corn Belt on Saturday and the entire belt on Sunday.

Gesser said temperatures would dip to normal-below normal early next week and a cold front would bring trace-1/2 inch of rain to abouot 20 percent of the corn belt. Temperatures are unlikely to dip low enough to pose a major threat to crops.

Most of the Corn Belt was frost free early Friday, with the most significant lows centered in Michigan, with temperatures falling to 22 degrees Fahrenheit in Grand Rapids and 26 degress in Lansing, Gesser said.

Light frosts were also reported in north-west Ohio and north-east Indiana with a low in Toledo, Ohio of 32 degrees, Dayton, Ohio of 34 degrees, South Bend, Indiana of 33 degrees and Fort Wayne, Indiana of 33 degrees.
"Last night was the coolest night in the E Belt thus far this season," Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis wrote in his daily weather update.
Davis forecast temperatures over the weekend would peak in the mid-60s F to the mid-70s F.
"Skies will be clear and dry, allowing for early harvesting to pick-up pace as well as late-growth to wind-up," Davis wrote.
A few showers are possible next week " but nothing of great significance nor in the heart of the belt," Smith Barney's Davis added.
